subject: Request: Clearsky carve-out for streaming TTFT vs polling token-rate
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearsky.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: ops@clearsky.ai, legal@clearsky.ai
Date: 2028-07-25T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Carve-out request: streaming endpoint TTFT vs polling token/sec

Markus —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we ramp the Clearsky embedding & chat agent into production (traffic starting this quarter) we need to finalize the SLA carve-outs before procurement will sign the reserved capacity contract. Two specific asks from our side: 

1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT) for the streaming endpoint: we need clarity on the metric you can guarantee for streaming (95th pct? 99th?), and whether TTFT is measured from request arrival at the gateway or after routing/re-encode.

2) Sustained token/sec expectations for streaming vs non-streaming (polling) endpoints. Our workload has many short queries that are latency-sensitive; we’re concerned the streaming tail will be worse under bursty traffic than the polling model.

Can Redwood provide: a) a proposed carve-out window (e.g., max 5% of requests allowed to exceed TTFT target during a 24h window), b) how you meter token/sec for billing/penalties, and c) any suggested mitigations (dedicated pool, pre-warming, hybrid fallback) we should include in the contract?

I attached our latency logs from the pilot (latency-logs-2028-07-25.zip) and the standard procurement exception form (redwood-sla-exception-form.pdf). Legal will need concrete SLO language to sign-off.

Appreciate a tight turnaround — procurement wants language by Monday.

— Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of Platform
Clearsky AI

From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearsky.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ops@clearsky.ai, legal@clearsky.ai
Date: 2028-07-26T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Carve-out request: streaming endpoint TTFT vs polling token/sec

Alyssa —

Thanks for the clear summary and the logs. We can work to get concrete SLO language. High-level response while I loop in Eng and Product: 

- TTFT definition: we typically define TTFT as the elapsed time from TCP/TLS termination at our public gateway to first token emitted by the model, reported at the 95th percentile per 24h. We can make the measurement at 99th for an enterprise addendum, but that changes the carve-out math.

- Token/sec measurement: for streaming endpoints we measure sustained token/sec as a per-connection metric starting at first-token and averaged over a 60s sliding window; for polling endpoints billing/penalty is measured as tokens delivered per-minute per-endpoint.

- Carve-out proposal: we can accept a limited exception window for live streaming: allow up to 3% of requests to exceed the TTFT target in any rolling 24h window, provided peak is caused by platform-wide congestion rather than per-customer misconfiguration. If Clearsky wants stricter guarantees we recommend a dedicated pool with reserved vGPU slots.

I’m adding Karthik and Lauren to confirm implementation/monitoring details and to draft specific clause language your Legal team can review.

Proposed next step: Karthik to propose SLO text + measurable tests by EOD tomorrow. If we can get that, I’ll hand to Contract Ops and loop in Sales Ops for pricing impact.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Growth — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearsky.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-26T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Carve-out request: streaming endpoint TTFT vs polling token/sec

Alyssa, Markus —

Digging into the test artifacts you sent. A few engineering clarifications and a proposed SLO snippet below. Please treat this as technical-first wording that Legal can adapt syntactically.

1) Measurement points: Redwood will report TTFT from the gateway that terminates customer TLS (ingress) to the first token emitted by the model runtime (eg. first byte of UTF-8 payload). This excludes client-side re-transmits and intermediate CDN caching.

2) Percentile & window: default is 95th percentile over a 24-hour rolling window. For enterprise carve-outs we can offer 99th pct at a 2x price uplift or require reserved capacity.

3) Token/sec measurement: for streaming endpoints we define sustained output-rate as tokens/sec measured per request starting at first-token and averaged over a 60-second sliding window; transient spikes shorter than 3s are ignored. For polling/non-streaming endpoints we measure tokens/minute delivered per endpoint invocation.

4) Proposed SLO text (technical): 
"TTFT_SLO: Redwood will ensure Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) <= 350ms at the 95th percentile per 24-hour window for Clearsky streaming endpoints served from the us-west region. Exclusion window: no more than 3% of requests may exceed 350ms within any rolling 24-hour period due to platform-wide capacity events. Customers operating without reserved capacity may be subject to higher variance; reserved pools offer tighter guarantees."

5) Mitigations we can operationalize: dedicated pool (reserved vGPU slots), pre-warmed hot-workers for predictable short queries, client-side retry + fallback to polling endpoint when first-token exceeds threshold, and a canary rollout for new model versions with auto-fallback.

6) Monitoring: we will provide token-level traces and per-request TTFT histograms to a shared S3/Drive location for the duration of the contract (30 days retention by default, extendable).

I’ll prepare a short appendix with the test harness (how we run synthetic steady-state and burst tests) and sample graphs — aiming to deliver by EOD.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearsky.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: legal@clearsky.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-27T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Carve-out request: streaming endpoint TTFT vs polling token/sec

Thanks Markus and Karthik — this is helpful and close to what Legal needs. A couple quick clarifications from our procurement/legal: 

- Is the 350ms TTFT tied to payload size? Our typical queries are ~20-40 tokens; can you confirm the baseline measurement assumes an empty prompt and vanilla model latency?

- For the 3% carve-out: would the exception be measured per-account or platform-wide? We need per-customer accountability (platform-wide events are OK, but per-tenant bursts should count against us).

- Can you confirm the export format for the TTFT histograms (we prefer NDJSON or a simple CSV) so we can plug into our monitoring?

If you can update the SLO text to mention payload-size assumptions and that the exclusion applies only to platform-wide incidents (not per-tenant overload), Legal can start redlining the clause.

Appreciate the fast follow.

— Alyssa

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@clearsky.ai>, markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, legal@clearsky.ai
Date: 2028-07-30T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Carve-out request: streaming endpoint TTFT vs polling token/sec

Alyssa —

Following up with the revised SLO language for Legal. We updated the clause to be explicit about payload assumptions and the scope of the carve-out. Pls see below (we can move to Contract Ops once Clearsky signs off).

Final suggested SLO clause (contract-friendly):
"Redwood guarantees a Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) of <= 350 milliseconds at the 95th percentile for streaming endpoints supporting Clearsky AI workloads in the US-West region. TTFT is measured from Redwood's TLS termination ingress to the emission of the first byte of model output. TTFT measurements assume request payloads up to 512 bytes (approximately 128 tokens). For request payloads exceeding this baseline, Redwood will provide an adjusted expectation in writing.

Exception carve-out: up to 3% of requests may exceed the TTFT target within any rolling 24-hour period, provided such exceedance is caused by platform-wide capacity events (e.g., multi-tenant congestion, upstream region failover). Per-tenant overloads or customer misconfigurations are not eligible for the carve-out and will be considered breaches of the provision unless mitigated via reserved capacity or agreed operational runbooks.

Token-rate metric: sustained token output-rate for streaming endpoints is measured per connection starting at first-token and averaged over a 60-second sliding window; transient spikes under 3 seconds are excluded from sustained-rate calculations. For non-streaming/polling endpoints, token delivery is measured as tokens per-minute per invocation.

Remediation & credits: In the event Redwood fails to meet the TTFT SLO outside of the defined carve-outs, Clearsky will be eligible for service credits as defined in Section X (credits scaled to the percentage of failing requests per month)."

Attachments: drafted clause (redwood-sla-exception-form.pdf) and sample TTFT histograms (latency-logs-2028-07-25.zip).

If that language looks good to Clearsky Legal, we’ll open a short Contract Ops ticket to produce a clean amendment.

— Lauren Bishop
Sr. Product Manager, Contracts & SLOs — Redwood Inference
